chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the arrows fall, the right of pre-emption is elevated."

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: Arrows (metaphor for shares or the act of drawing lots/distribution)
key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption (the right to buy a property before a stranger)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'when the arrows fall' in the context of Islamic pre-emption law?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the temporal activation of *al-shuf'ah* (pre-emption), using the metaphor of 'arrows falling' to signify the precise moment of sale or share distribution. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on protecting co-owners' rights against arbitrary alienation of shared property, ensuring that the preemptive right is exercised immediately upon the transaction's completion.
